Stephen Thorne's charge can sometimes be slowly away but, with this drop in class, the eight-year-old may be able to get away with it. Conor Cusack rode his first winner in Limerick for Henry De Bromhead on Saturday and the 10lb claimer is once more entrusted with Catena Zapata. He has performed below par on his last couple of starts, but the application of first-time blinkers may spark a revival. Both Captain Hanley and Summer Island ran in Ayr on their latest starts, with the latter performing with credit on the back of strong market support.

selections.comment: National Stakes entries provide some clues in this open affair, with both DIAL ME IN and A Boy Named Susie holding the engagement. Experience may prove valuable so there is marginal preference for Joseph O'Brien's contender, who came from back in the field to just get up on the line in a Leopardstown maiden. The son of Awtaad was clearly learning on the job, suggesting he should progress, with the step up to a mile being of benefit too. The 185,000gns yearling Acclamatic showed some promise when fourth in a Naas barrier trial and should improve for that experience. Wyman is a son of Australia who cost 100,000 euros as a yearling and is worth watching, with the market potentially providing some insight.

selections.comment: RED LETTER sets the clear standard and should be able to get back to winning ways after narrowly losing out in a race of similar quality. Her two-year-old form obviously reads very well, running well on two occasions behind Irish 1,000 Guineas heroine Lake Victoria. Joseph O'Brien runs three in the race, with the apparent first-string Wannabe Royal, although she was held behind the selection on her latest start and it is hard to see a reversal of that form. The Ballydoyle contingent is headed by Ecstatic, who never figured up in grade in the Ribblesdale, but the drop in trip may aid her cause. The ever-consistent Fiery Lucy can go close once more in this company.

The Tom McCourt-trained gelding appeared to have a bit in hand when beating better-fancied stablemate Maxwell Smart, with Tassarolo about eight lengths back in fourth, and can score again off his revised mark. The latter gets a 1lb pull for a length and a neck. Coolagh Magic looks the most solid alternative with Jimmy Knocker just preferred to Court Of Seesion. Mollymook looks most interestiong of the rest

selections.comment: NOBLE GUEST can show his latest running to be all wrong and bounce back and take this. Before a latest blip he was in fine form wit a good second at Lingield on turf over the extended seven furlongs and before that had trouble in running when sixth at Kempton over 7f. A repeat of those efforts would make him the one to beat and it's encouraging his best run arguably came over course and distance on fast ground on second career run. Daring Legend is a serious threat having gone so close last time under similar conditions to today at Doncaster and has a win and a place from two runs over this course and distance. Michaeal Appleby's charge has been incredibly reliable off late and shouldn't be far away again. Stardancer has a bit to make up on the chief protagonists but showed enough on handicap debut last time off a layoff to suggest he's capable of making a mark in this kind of company and the first try at seven furlongs suited well. He's a serious danger to all if he can build on his comeback run as seems likely

However the form of that return has had knocks and she could be vulnerable to the unexposed LOVE SONNET who finished powerfully when making a winning handicap debut over 11f suggesting that this longer trip could bring out more. She had a next time out winner in behind that day and the booking of Keane again hints another big run is expected. Surrey Force needed the run on his recent stable debut but will also be in the mix if back to the level of his UK form.
